title: Implicit Mapping via Untyped Reflection/Dictionaries
pattern: Mapping boundary DTO values to domain objects using generic, untyped reflection, runtime dictionaries, or string-based field name comparisons.
why_bad: It eliminates the safety of static compiled type systems. Renaming a field in a domain struct compiled successfully but causes quiet, runtime bugs or data drops when the mapper fails to locate the string key.
detection: Core boundary mapping logic relying on string-keyed hash maps or generic runtime reflection APIs to copy values into domain struct fields.
counterexample: Explicit, compiler-checked structural mapping implementations (such as compiled code generated automatically by macros like `serde`).
source: *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* by Martin Fowler (p. 353, "Assembling a Data Transfer Object").
